newsitem.title: SPAIN: Dealers suspect BoS slowing peseta gains.
newsitem.headline: Dealers suspect BoS slowing peseta gains.

text.p: The Bank of Spain was hindering the peseta's appreciation on Monday, braking its progress beyond 84.05 per mark, dealers said.
The Bank of Spain could not be reached for comment.
"There have been rumours since the open that the Bank of Spain is intervening through third parties to break the appreciation of the currrency," said a dealer.
Dealers said they had not seen the Bank of Spain intervene, but added that the peseta should have broken the 84.00 level with ease given the mark's weariness and hot demand for Spanish bonds.
At 0755 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.07/08 per mark after opening at 84.02/05 and closing Friday at 84.10/12.
Dealers said they suspected the Bank of Spain was intervening at 84.05 per mark.
They added that the peseta's firmness was raising pressure on the Bank of Spain to lower its key money market intervention rate from 7.25 percent on Tuesday at the regular repo tender.
